 Constellation Completes Calpine Transaction 
 Constellation
 134,087 followers
 8mo
 Report this post
 America’s premier energy company has officially arrived. 
We’re thrilled to announce that our combination with Calpine is complete, creating America’s largest energy producer serving 2.5 million customers nationwide. 
This is about far more than scale. Together, our 55 gigawatts of generating capacity, innovative products and services and industry-leading talent will better serve our customers and communities coast to coast while meeting the challenge to supply U.S. homes and businesses with reliable energy, even as demand continues to rise.
We’re built to power the nation’s growth with dependable, clean American energy. Our new chapter starts now.

 Great news to share this AM that Constellation has officially merged with Calpine , creating the largest electricity producer in the United States. By combining Constellation’s zero-emission nuclear fleet with Calpine’s best‑in‑class natural gas and geothermal generation, our newly unified organization delivers 55 GW of capacity and serves 2.5 million retail and business customers. This milestone further expands our strategy of driving innovation that supports electrification, data centers, and emerging industries throughout the nation.

The conference draws power producers, utilities, OEMs and large-scale energy users from around the world. The conference looks at the future of power generation and includes focus on what its website references as "The Total Energy Mix: Powering the Future, ensuring that all energy sources are considered in the journey toward sustainability."

 This week, we presented to members of the British Ports Association on how battery energy storage can support ports with their electrification strategies.
With ports under increasing pressure to decarbonise while managing rising energy demands and costs, battery storage offers a practical solution. Beyond operational flexibility and cost savings, recent regulatory changes have opened up new revenue opportunities that significantly improve project economics.
The session covered practical considerations for port operators looking at battery storage to help optimise power and implement sustainable energy systems.
Thanks to the BPA for hosting us and to everyone who joined the discussion. If you'd like to explore how battery storage could work for your port operations, get in touch with our team Robert Moore and Jonathan Mann
